newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Second group of Italian troops arrive at airport.
newsitem.headline: Second group of Italian troops arrive at airport.

text.p: An Italian military transport plane carrying advance units of a multinational security force arrived at Tirana airport on Friday, eyewitnesses said.

The transport plane carrying parachute troopers arrived at about 9 a.m. (0700 GMT), about one hour after an Italian Navy transport ship pulled into the Albanian port of Durres, about 40 km (25 miles) west of Tirana.

Journalists at Tirana airport, which is 25 km (15 miles) west of the centre of the Albanian capital, said about 25 to 28 Italian soliders and three Italian minivans came off the Italian aircraft shortly after it landed.

Along with a contingent of about 20 Italian soliders who arrived on a ship in Durres, the Italian troops form the vanguard of a 6,000-strong U.N.-backed force due to begin arriving in Albania on Monday.
The force, the first of its kind led by Italy, is on a mission to assist the delivery of relief aid to Albania, brought to the brink of collapse by an armed insurrection last month.

Troops from France, Greece, Spain, Turkey and Romania are also in the force. Austria and Denmark are also considering participation. More than 200 poeple have been killed since rebels took control of the south last month in an eruption of anger over a number of failed pyramid savings schemes.
